preamble: Regressive manner assimilation turns the voiceless uvular stop /q/ into the uvular nasal [ɴ] before a nasal consonant, while the uvular place of articulation is kept. The best-documented case is Eastern Canadian Inuktitut, where a stem-final q followed by a nasal-initial suffix is written r and pronounced [ɴ] (umiaq 'boat' + -mut > umiarmut [umiaɴmut] 'to a boat'); some analyses phonemicize the nasalized uvular as an allophone of /ʁ/ rather than of /q/. Northern (Taz) Selkup has the same allophony: [ɴ] is the realization of /q/ before a nasal, just as [ʀ] is its realization before a liquid. The rarity of uvular stops and of the uvular nasal itself keeps this shift cross-linguistically uncommon.

examples.note: Mallon describes [ɴ] as the nasal allophone of q and states that no Inuk pronounces the r of umiarmut as a plain voiced fricative; the orthography writes q before voiceless consonants and r before voiced and nasal ones.
Descriptions of Taz Selkup (Helimski 1998; Kazakevič 2022) list [ɴ] and [ʀ] as allophones of /q/ before nasals and liquids respectively; no individual word forms were verified.
